sections.title: The library of materials, the contact sheet
sections.need: Every standard document of the base library (S4a) renders through the reverse conversion table and the wgpu host; the sheet is the human gate: the metals tell apart, gold is gold, the lacquer is red, the leaf is green. The legend beside it names every cell.

pictures.feature: the base library, 26 documents, forward path
pictures.caption: content/materials/standard/ in roster order, six to a row, each cell labelled with its family and title (a long title is cut with a dot; contact-sheet.json has it whole): metal (base, aluminium, brass, chrome, copper, gold, iron, metal plate, silver, brushed steel), dielectric (base, brown planks, ceramic, glossy plastic, matte plastic), coated (base, painted red), rough (base, brick wall, cobblestone floor, concrete, rubber), emissive (base, panel), cutout (base, leaf); contact-sheet.json is the legend. The emissive pair do not glow: the wgpu host carries no emission term, so they render as their dark base colour; anisotropy, specular colour and specular occlusion are the table's losses, so brushed steel is iron here; the four T3 documents show their families' constants, since this host samples no texture yet (T3b)

sections.title: The texture cook: frequency separation
sections.need: The owner's technique as a cook operation: the low-pass and the high-pass of a sourced colour map recombine to the source under a linear-light blend, within one 8-bit step; the macro colour can be stored at a few texels and the detail at full resolution.

pictures.feature: the source colour map (Poly Haven cobblestone_floor_04, CC0, 1K, shown at 512)
pictures.caption: the post's own example set, cooked outside the repository as T2's proof; the set itself lands with T3

pictures.feature: the low-pass (sigma 8, radius 16), wrap-padded so it tiles
pictures.caption: what the macro colour map carries; the cook stores it at 64x64

pictures.feature: the high-pass about mid-grey, the detail map T_cobblestone_floor_04_DH
pictures.caption: 8-bit quantised, as written; neutral grey where the source equals its low-pass

pictures.feature: the recombination, saturate(low + 2 * high - 1)
pictures.caption: the manifest measures it: error max 0.0039 (one 8-bit step), mean 0.0020, 440 of 1048576 texels clipped

pictures.feature: the brick wall's source colour map (brick_wall_001, 2K, shown at 512)
pictures.caption: the committed set, separated with --compress

pictures.feature: the brick wall's high-pass about mid-grey
pictures.caption: the mortar lines and the brick texture; the low frequency is in the macro

pairs.caption: the source against its recombination: the difference is the 8-bit quantisation of the high-pass and nothing else
